  margin-inline-end: var(--s-3);
  background: radial-gradient(
    circle at 35% 30%,
    var(--accent-2),
    var(--accent));
  border-radius: 50%;
}

Type flows around the shape instead of the invisible box, so the words tuck in close and the little round thing here finally looks like it belongs rather than sitting in an empty rectangle like a cat in a carrier. Resize the window and the lines re-wrap, which is the fun part.

instances.html:
CSS :user-invalid for live validation

Style fields after the user has interacted and left them invalid—no JavaScript required.

:user-invalid matches an input only after the user has tried to submit or blurred it with invalid content. It's the polite sibling of :invalid, which fires too eagerly.

Use it to add a red border and a helper message. The browser won't show the message until the field is actually wrong.

input:user-invalid {
  border-color: var(--bad);
}
input:user-invalid + .hint {
  display: block;
  color: var(--bad);
}
.hint { display: none; }

Supported in modern browsers as of 2023. Fall back to :invalid for older ones if you must.

instances.html:
CSS text-emphasis for elegant emphasis

Draw small marks above or below text—great for East Asian typography or playful accents.

text-emphasis adds repeating symbols over each character. You control the mark with text-emphasis-style and its color with text-emphasis-color.

It's especially handy for Japanese emphasis dots, but works for any script. The marks won't affect line height.

em {
  text-emphasis: dot var(--accent);
  text-emphasis-position: under right;
  font-style: normal; /* optional */
}

The position value controls where the mark appears—above or below—and its alignment.

instances.title: CSS caret-color for custom cursors
instances.html:
CSS caret-color for custom cursors

Tint the text insertion cursor to match your accent—subtle but delightful.

The caret-color property sets the color of the blinking cursor in inputs, textareas, and contenteditable elements. It defaults to the text color, but you can make it any color.

Set it to auto to keep the browser default, or to a custom value for a branded touch.

input, textarea {
  caret-color: var(--accent);
}

/* Or match the text color for simplicity */
input { caret-color: currentColor; }

Works everywhere except very old browsers. No fallback needed.

instances.title: CSS font-synthesis for faux bold prevention
instances.html:
CSS font-synthesis for faux bold prevention

Stop browsers from faking bold or italic when a font lacks those faces.

With font-synthesis you can tell the browser not to synthesize bold, italic, or small-caps. This keeps your typography true to the typeface, avoiding ugly faux styles.

Set it on the element or globally. It's a small win for design purists.

body {
  font-synthesis: none; /* no faux bold/italic */
}

/* Or prevent only weight synthesis */
h1 {
  font-synthesis-weight: none;
}

If the font has a real bold, it will still be used. This only blocks fake ones.

instances.title: CSS all: unset for resetting styles
user_requests: how to remove all styles from element
instances.html:
CSS all: unset for resetting styles

Wipe an element's styles clean—back to inherited or initial values.

all is a shorthand for every property. all: unset resets to inherited values if the property inherits, or initial if not. It's a sledgehammer for style isolation.

Commonly used on components that need to break free from parent styles, like a custom button inside a styled paragraph.

.clean-slate {
  all: unset;
}

/* Or reset to initial values */
.reset-to-initial {
  all: initial;
}

Note: all doesn't affect custom properties or direction/unicode-bidi.

instances.title: CSS text-size-adjust for mobile legibility
user_requests: prevent text resizing on mobile css
instances.html:
CSS text-size-adjust for mobile legibility

Control automatic text inflation on mobile devices—keep your layout predictable.

Mobile browsers sometimes enlarge text in wide blocks to make it readable. text-size-adjust lets you disable or customize that behaviour.

Set it to 100% to prevent inflation, or none to disable entirely. Use sparingly—it can harm accessibility.

body {
  text-size-adjust: 100%;
}

/* For a specific container */
.card {
  text-size-adjust: none;
}

Best used on components where layout stability matters more than browser guessing.
